ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached image shows a 3D cube with three visible drilled openings: one on the top face, one on the front face, and one on the right face. The openings are rectangular/square tunnel cross-sections, and the shading inside suggests the tunnels pass through the cube in three perpendicular directions and meet in the same central 1 by 1 by 1 region. Reasoning: The original cube is 3 by 3 by 3, so its volume is 27 cubic units. Since it weighs 810 grams, the density is 810 / 27 = 30 grams per cubic unit. Each drilled hole is a 1 by 1 by 3 rectangular parallelepiped, so each has volume 3. Three holes would naively remove 3 + 3 + 3 = 9 cubic units. However, the three tunnels overlap at the central unit cube. Using inclusion-exclusion, the removed volume is 3 + 3 + 3 - 1 - 1 - 1 + 1 = 7 cubic units. Thus the remaining volume is 27 - 7 = 20 cubic units. The remaining weight is 20 * 30 = 600 grams.

method.method_draft: Use volume and inclusion-exclusion. First describe the image: the cube has three drilled rectangular holes visible on the top, front, and right faces, indicating three mutually perpendicular 1 by 1 by 3 tunnels that pass through the cube and overlap in the same central 1 by 1 by 1 region. From the text, the original cube is 3 by 3 by 3 and weighs 810 g, so its volume is 27 cubic units and its density is 810/27 = 30 g per cubic unit. Each tunnel has volume 1*1*3 = 3, so the naive removed volume is 9. Because the three tunnels intersect at the central unit cube, subtract the overcount: the union of removed material has volume 3+3+3 - 3 pairwise overlaps of volume 1 + 1 triple overlap = 7. The remaining volume is 27 - 7 = 20, so the remaining weight is 20*30 = 600 g.

method.method_draft: Use unit-cube counting. First describe the image: the top, front, and side openings show three perpendicular tunnels through the 3 by 3 by 3 cube, each one unit wide, aligned so that they pass through the middle of the cube. Divide the large cube into 27 unit cubes. From the text, the whole cube weighs 810 g, so each unit cube weighs 810/27 = 30 g. Count the unit cubes removed by the tunnels as a 3D cross: the central cube is removed, plus one unit cube extending from it toward each of the six faces, for 7 removed unit cubes total.
